title: Terminal and Vector
premise: Paloma Blackwood, a memory-smuggler running contraband past orbital customs, discovers his name on the manifest of a ship that never flew—a vessel erased from every registry, carrying a stolen archive of judicial memories that could topple the colonial authority that killed his family. Hunted by both the Authority's enforcers and the smugglers who sold him out, he races toward the relay at the edge of dead space to broadcast the archive before the jump window closes, aided by Sefa Idris, a disgraced customs officer torn between duty and conscience. At the relay, Paloma must choose between transmitting the archive—which will expose him as the thief and end his life of invisibility—and escaping clean. He transmits, sacrificing his anonymity and nearly his life, because justice outside the law is still justice; in the aftermath, stripped of cargo, ship, and cover identity, he finds something he never smuggled for himself: a future shared with Sefa.
about_author: Jonah Sandoval is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to voices cross empty water before turning to fiction about voices crossing emptier space. They write from a coastal town where the fog comes in on schedule, like a jump window.

chapters.title: Contraband Heart
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A routine smuggling run through Halcyon Gate customs establishes his world: hidden memory-shards in coolant lines, bribed inspectors, seven years of careful invisibility. The emotional beat is weary competence—he's good at this and tired of it—until dockside gossip mentions a ghost ship called the Vesperine that supposedly never flew.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Pulling favors from a records broker, Paloma finds the Vesperine's manifest bearing his own name as registered owner—a ship decommissioned before he ever left Earth. Someone built him a paper history. Fear replaces fatigue: invisibility was an illusion someone else maintained.

chapters.title: Sefa
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Customs officer Sefa Idris, demoted after refusing to falsify an inspection, is assigned to investigate the Vesperine anomaly. She recognizes Paloma's name from a cold case—the Blackwood family deaths ruled accidental. Her beat: duty pulling against a doubt she can't unfeel.

chapters.title: Shard and Shadow
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He breaks into a dead storage bay and finds the Vesperine itself, hull-cold, its hold packed with memory-shards: testimony from judges, witnesses, victims—evidence the Authority buried when it razed the Blackwood district. The beat is grief detonating into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Shards Remember
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, intercut with shard-playback. Experiencing fragments of his mother's final testimony, Paloma learns she wasn't collateral damage—she was the witness the purge was meant to erase. Emotional beat: love for the dead sharpened into obligation to the living.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. His records broker sells him out to Kestrel Vane, a smuggler-kingpin who wants the archive's black-market value. Paloma escapes the ambush but loses his safehouse. Beat: the cost of trusting anyone in contested orbits.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa boards the Vesperine ahead of her superiors and finds it already disturbed—and finds Paloma waiting in the dark with a shard pressed to the ship's playback port. Instead of arresting him, she listens to thirty seconds of a judge confessing to ordering the purge. Beat: her duty cracks.

chapters.title: Two Fugitives
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Paloma and Sefa strike an uneasy bargain: she'll get him past the cordon if he gives her the full archive afterward—for her own tribunal, not his escape. Neither trusts the other. Beat: two people negotiating trust with weapons loose.

chapters.title: Cordon Break
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A brutal run through Halcyon Gate under false transponder codes, Sefa feeding him inspection windows from inside. They clear the cordon by seconds, but her badge ID is logged. Beat: exhilaration curdling—she's burned now too.

chapters.title: Dead Space Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Shared POV aboard the Vesperine. The only relay that can broadcast the archive sits at the edge of dead space; the next jump window closes in nine days, and Vane's hunters are three days behind. Fuel math says they can't outrun them. Beat: claustrophobic dread and reluctant intimacy.

chapters.title: Fuel Is Memory
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. To extend their range, Paloma must sell shards—pieces of the dead's testimony—to scavengers who'll play them for entertainment. Each sale buys hours of thrust and costs him a piece of his mother's voice. Beat: survival priced in sacrilege.

chapters.title: The Tribunal That Never Was
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Flashback chapter: Sefa's career, the falsified inspection she refused, the mentor who abandoned her, why justice-through-institutions failed her long before Paloma did. Beat: understanding why she's really here—not for the law, but for what the law promised her.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Vane catches them at a fuel depot and offers a deal: hand over the archive, walk away rich, invisible again. Paloma refuses—and realizes Vane didn't build the manifest to frame him. Vane built it to find him. Beat: the trap was always personal.

chapters.title: Burn and Run
chapters.summary: Action chapter, alternating POV. Depot firefight; Sefa takes a graze shielding Paloma; they lose half their fuel and all their margin. In the quiet after, Paloma admits why he never let anyone close. Beat: love admitted aloud in the wreckage.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Days of coasting through dead space with failing systems and no traffic. They play the remaining shards together—not as evidence but as eulogy. Sefa tells him the truth about the tribunal she wanted. Beat: tenderness as defiance.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They detect Vane's ship shadowing them silent, running dark. Paloma baits a decoy transmission while Sefa preps the relay approach. Beat: hunter and hunted trading patience, the tension of being watched by nothing visible.

chapters.title: Window Opening
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They reach the relay with six hours of window left—but the relay needs manual authorization from a live customs credential. Only Sefa has one. Using it will sign her name to the broadcast forever. Beat: duty and conscience finally facing each other across a console.

chapters.title: Vane at the Door
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Vane boards during the upload, offering one last trade: stop the broadcast and Paloma gets his old life back, scrubbed and real. Paloma answers with the truth—that the life was always someone else's fiction. Beat: the climax of identity, choosing exposure over erasure.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. Sefa authorizes with her credential as Vane's crew breaches the relay; Paloma holds the line physically while the archive streams to every open receiver in contested space. Vane dies in the crossfire of his own hired guns once the evidence makes him worthless. Beat: catharsis through cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The archive lands like a bomb: tribunals reopen, officials fall, and both their names are public record. Sefa faces suspension and chooses resignation over reinstatement in a corrupted service. Beat: justice achieved, institutions unchanged, and no regret.

chapters.title: Manifest, Amended
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Stripped of ship, cargo, and cover, Paloma stands in the same dockside bar where the story began, now legally named on a registry he chose himself. An offer arrives to fly again—legitimately, or almost. Beat: grief settling into peace.

chapters.title: Terminal and Vector
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing chapter. Paloma and Sefa take a small contract haul together, no contraband, no ghosts in the hold—just two people who chose each other over safety. Final image: the jump window opening, and this time walking through it side by side. Beat: earned hope.
